positioning.name: Marc Lefèvre

hero.eyebrow: Customer Avatar · AI governance / risk / security
hero.headline: Marc Lefèvre: the release-control buyer, without invented biography.
hero.lead: The working name and role make the segment concrete. Everything that is not evidenced—age, family, individual income, education, exact personal geography, media habits or favourite brands—stays explicitly unasserted.
hero.proof_line: The source role is Responsable gouvernance, risque ou sécurité IA. The commercial problem is bounded: AI systems can act before the organisation can reconstruct who authorised what, under which controls, against which release evidence.

mandate.before: AI code, agents, connectors and infrastructure approach release while security remains a late report.
mandate.after: Security, policy and supply-chain checks become explicit promotion gates with evidence and rollback criteria.
mandate.decision_role: Decision-maker or advocate depending on the organisation; final budget authority remains to validate.
mandate.evidence_status: Role model + current admitted EU/EUG; buyer psychology still requires field validation.

triggers.headline: What pushes this buyer away from the status quo.
points: Release velocity collides with assurance: Security evidence arrives as a late reconstruction instead of part of the release path.
Agent authority widens the control surface: Tools, credentials, data access and side effects change what “safe enough” means.
Audit evidence is repeatedly rebuilt: Each audit, renewal or customer request becomes another evidence-collection project.
Applicable obligations are time-bound: Where legal requirements apply, missing scope or evidence can no longer be treated as a maturity exercise.

consequences.headline: The object to control is authority, not only model output.
points: Prompting is not the control plane: Consequential action requires enforcement outside the model when the risk boundary requires it.
Source code is not the whole surface: Network reach, identities, tools, connectors, memory and reachable data also shape exposure.
Human approval is not self-validating: The approval context and the consequence of the approved action remain part of the risk model.

buyer.headline: Human enough to write for; bounded enough not to fabricate.

qualification.headline: What must be true before this buyer can defend a yes.
must_haves: Evidence bound to the release artifact.
Integration with the existing delivery chain.
deal_killers: No access to the evidence boundary.
Report-only engagement where enforcement is the real requirement.
qualification.service_expectation: Assurance + implementation + handoff. The consultant can design controls, gates and evidence; the work does not replace the client’s accountable authority, regulator, auditor or certification body.
qualification.to_validate: Price threshold, procurement constraints, budget owner, vendor restrictions, observed objections and the exact decision-maker / advocate / champion split.

proposition.headline: Risk → Policy → Test → Evidence → Promote / Block.
proposition.intro: The commercial mechanism is deliberately narrower than a promise of “safer AI”: translate a bounded risk statement into controls the delivery chain can enforce and a release record another accountable person can inspect later.

offers.headline: AI Security, Assurance & DevSecOps — a release-control mandate.
offers.price_boundary: Price and procurement assumptions are not part of the avatar until first-party sales evidence supports them.
offers.core_engagement: 3–6 months, typically 2–4 days/week. Scope is assembled from threat modelling, runtime boundaries, release gates, supply-chain controls, evidence design and team handoff.

deliverables.headline: Concrete objects the buyer can inspect and hand over.

items.title: AI attack-surface inventory
items.body: Agents, tools, connectors, reachable data, secrets, identities, owners and external systems.

items.title: Release gate
items.body: Named controls, thresholds, blocking behaviour, exception path and uncovered residual scope.

items.title: Release decision record
items.body: Control results, artifact/version, exceptions, residual risk and accountable approver.

before-after.headline: The transformation is explicit across all five Customer Avatar axes.

axes.before: Late report; fragmented release evidence; implicit authority.
axes.after: Explicit promotion gates, ownership, evidence, exceptions and rollback criteria.
Confidence that a release decision can be explained and replayed.

axes.before: Repeated evidence requests and late security review compete with delivery.
axes.after: Control failures and exceptions enter a defined release workflow.
Co-owner of release eligibility and residual-risk decisions.
Bounded authority with attributable, reviewable decisions.

results.headline: What this role model is trying to add—not a promise that the offer will cause it.

aspirations.title: Provable controls
aspirations.body: Policies expressed as owned controls with evidence and explicit residual-risk decisions.

aspirations.title: Risk-based release eligibility
aspirations.body: State what may enter production, under which controls and what blocks promotion.

aspirations.title: Less repeated assurance friction
aspirations.body: Reuse evidence and owner workflows instead of reconstructing the same release context repeatedly.

acceptance_tests.label: Acceptance · testable
acceptance_tests.title: A deliberately failing control blocks the target artifact.
acceptance_tests.body: The gate changes promotion when its predicate fails.

acceptance_tests.label: Acceptance · reconstructable
acceptance_tests.title: A selected release resolves to one decision record.
acceptance_tests.body: Artifact, policy, evidence, exception and approval remain joinable.

acceptance_tests.label: Acceptance · transferable
acceptance_tests.title: The team can add a control and run the exception path.
acceptance_tests.body: Handoff succeeds using source-controlled configuration and runbooks.

scope.headline: Included, excluded, dependent on the client.
explicitly_out: ISO, SOC or regulatory certification decisions.

process.headline: Four phases. Four usable stopping points.

phases.body: Inventory agents, connectors, credentials and reachable data. Output: boundary + threat model.
Translate controls into blocking conditions. Output: live release gate.
Bind promotion to policy, results, exceptions, artifact identity and approver.
The team adds a control and executes an exception path without the consultant.

modules.headline: Select modules from the risk boundary, not from a fixed checklist.

modules.title: Threat modelling
modules.body: Objective, action surface, reachable services, prompts/context, failure scenarios and red lines.

modules.title: Agent isolation & authority
modules.body: Capability boundaries, network restrictions, credential scope, escalation and external authorization where justified.

modules.title: Supply chain & promotion
modules.body: SBOM, dependencies, images, secrets, policy predicates, exceptions and rollback criteria.

modules.title: Observability & release evidence
modules.body: Runtime traces, sandbox logs, artifact identity, decision journals and accountable approval.

intersection.headline: Marc is not the whole buying system.
intersection.intro: NeoFort currently models eight recurring collaborators. This is a proposed organisational model, not observed frequency data and not a claim that all eight roles exist in every account.
intersection.boundary: Decision-maker / Advocate / Champion classification and final budget authority remain TO_VALIDATE per organisation.

commitments.headline: Guarantee the work product, never an authority’s decision.

commitments.title: Scope before billing
commitments.body: Scope, exclusions, dependencies and acceptance criteria are written first.

commitments.title: Rework against criteria
commitments.body: A deliverable failing agreed acceptance criteria is reworked against them.

commitments.title: Reversibility
commitments.body: Code, configuration, schemas, decisions and journals are handed over.

commitments.title: Human decision boundary
commitments.body: Each consequential use case states where automation stops and named approval begins.

questions.headline: Objections are hypotheses until the sales record confirms them.

faq.q: Will a blocking gate slow the team?
faq.a: It can. The design question is whether the risk justifies the block and whether a traceable exception path exists.

faq.q: Must we replace Jenkins, GitLab or GitHub Actions?
faq.a: No. The policy is designed around the delivery chain in place unless migration is itself the decision.
No single control is assumed sufficient. Approval context, authority and runtime enforcement are designed together.

faq.q: What budget does this avatar have?
faq.a: TO_VALIDATE. No individual income, departmental budget or price threshold is inferred from the role title.

engagement.headline: Bring one decision, one critical asset and one buyer-evidence signal.
engagement.intro: The first conversation should validate both the technical mandate and one Customer Avatar uncertainty: a real objection, a budget owner, an information source, or a verbatim. That turns the persona from a useful model into progressively observed market context.

inputs.label: 01 · Decision
inputs.body: The release, audit, renewal or launch event that has to move.

inputs.label: 02 · Boundary
inputs.body: The asset, agent or system whose authority, dependencies and reachable data matter.

inputs.label: 03 · Buyer evidence
inputs.body: One observed objection, stakeholder, content source, quote or procurement fact.
